Multinomial Third Derivatives

Source: R/mv_higher.R
distrib_deriv3.MultinomialDistrib.Rd

Computes every third derivative of the log-mass in the parameters, in closed form. Up to a constant in the counts the log-mass is \(\sum_j y_j \log p_j\). On the additive log-ratio chart of parameters7::simplex() this equals \(\sum_{j<p} y_j\eta_j - N\,\mathrm{LSE}(\eta)\), with \(N\) the total of the row, so every derivative of order two or more is \(-N\) times a joint cumulant of the indicators of the categorical law (see mn_cumulant()). The cumulant is a sum of products of probabilities, computed without dividing by one, so it stays finite when a probability underflows. On another chart each term depends on one coordinate of the simplex and the chain rule reduces to a univariate partition sum per coordinate, with $$f^{(m)}(p) = (-1)^{m-1}(m-1)!\,p^{-m},$$ weighted by the counts.

Arguments

distrib

A MultinomialDistrib object, from multinomial_distrib().

y

A numeric matrix with one row per observation and one column per category, where each row is a vector of counts that sum to distrib@size.

theta

A named list of parameters, where each component is a single number: probs_alr1, ..., probs_alr(p-1).

expected

Logical of length 1. When TRUE the expectation is returned, in closed form (see Details). Defaults to FALSE.

scale

One of "parameter" (the default) or "link". The method returns the parameter scale and the generic applies the link scale to its result.

method

NULL: the generic applies an object before dispatching on the family, so this method receives NULL and returns the closed form. See expected_derivative_methods.

...

Unused, and accepted so that the signature matches the generic's.

Value

A named list of numeric vectors of length \(n\), keyed and ordered as deriv_names(distrib@params, 3). At \(p = 3\) there are four components, because the simplex has \(p - 1\) free values. With expected = TRUE every vector is constant.

Details

With expected = TRUE the expectation is exact. The derivatives are linear in the counts, so the method replaces each count by its expectation \(n p_j\). On the additive log-ratio chart this replaces \(N\) by \(n\), and the result equals the observed value at every row on the support.

Notation

\(p_j\) is the probability of category \(j\), \(y_j\) its count, \(n\) the number of trials, \(\eta\) the simplex's free vector and \(\ell\) the log-mass of one observation.

See also

distrib_deriv4.MultinomialDistrib() for the next order, multinomial_higher() for the shared engine, mn_cumulant() for the cumulants, and distrib_deriv3() for the generic.

Examples

d <- multinomial_distrib(3, size = 10)
theta <- list(probs_alr1 = 0.4, probs_alr2 = -0.3)
set.seed(2)
y <- distrib_rng(d, 5, theta)

d3 <- distrib_deriv3(d, y, theta)
vapply(d3, sum, numeric(1))
#> probs_alr1_probs_alr1_probs_alr1 probs_alr1_probs_alr1_probs_alr2 
#>                       -0.9570972                        0.4072999 
#> probs_alr1_probs_alr2_probs_alr2 probs_alr2_probs_alr2_probs_alr2 
#>                        2.8642703                       -4.7842481 

# The result is compared with a central difference of the Hessian.
h <- 1e-4
tp <- theta; tp$probs_alr2 <- tp$probs_alr2 + h
tm <- theta; tm$probs_alr2 <- tm$probs_alr2 - h
c(exact = sum(d3[["probs_alr1_probs_alr1_probs_alr2"]]),
  stencil = (sum(distrib_hessian(d, y, tp)[["probs_alr1_probs_alr1"]]) -
             sum(distrib_hessian(d, y, tm)[["probs_alr1_probs_alr1"]])) /
            (2 * h))
#>     exact   stencil 
#> 0.4072999 0.4072999 

# The expectation equals the sum over the finite support.
sup <- mv_support(d, theta)
w <- distrib_pdf(d, sup, theta)
c(expected = distrib_deriv3(d, y, theta, expected = TRUE)[[1]][1],
  sum = sum(w * distrib_deriv3(d, sup, theta)[[1]]))
#>   expected        sum 
#> -0.1914194 -0.1914194
